pageCache.pageTitle: Bampton C.E. Primary School - Burford Partnership
pageCache.text:
Burford Partnership
The Burford Partnership of Schools and Transition to Secondary School
To ensure the move to secondary school is smooth and enjoyable, Bampton Primary School continues to work closely with our partnership school Burford Secondary School. Burford organise enrichment days to which all of our year 5 children are invited and senior leaders come and talk to parents of year 5 pupils. Since Oxfordshire County Council made changes to the free bus entitlement for Y7 pupils we are also working with Carterton Community College who offer transition days for those pupils moving to their school. We have also worked with other local secondary schools on a smooth transition package if parents have selected an alternative school for Y7.
Bampton Primary School works in close partnership with Burford Secondary and eight local primary schools. This strong Partnership exists to develop curriculum, cultural and sporting links as well as provide professional development opportunities for our staff.
The Headteachers from the Burford Partnership of schools meet regularly. There is a programme of activities for children in KS2 to support the transition process. The Burford Partnership also organise a range of PE festivals and tournaments for children of all ages to participate in.
For those children with Special Educational Needs or disabilities we liaise with the SENDCo from the secondary schools in order to support a smooth transition that supports provision to meet their needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bampton C.E. Primary School - Outdoor Explorers
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Explorers
About Outdoor Explorer
Outdoor Explorer is based on the Forest School ethos which embraces the outdoors as a stimulating learning environment focussed on your child’s learning needs and interests rather than particular learning outcomes. Your children will explore and experience the natural world, on a regular basis during our Outdoor Explorer sessions. These sessions aim to offer a unique way of building self-esteem and confidence in addition to learning new life skills and promoting independence, through hands on learning experiences.
Outdoor Explorer will usually take place in the school grounds.
The log circle and fire pit can be used to refresh the ‘Outdoor Explorer’ rules, sing songs, read stories and enjoy a cup of hot chocolate with toasted marshmallows!
We have qualified staff who are trained in planning and delivering outdoor learning experiences.
All activities are fully risk assessed.
Inclement Weather Procedure
There is no such thing as bad weather, only inappropriate clothing Sir Ranulph Fiennes
The weather and the seasons provide a rich variety of play experiences so Outdoor Explorer sessions will take place in most weather conditions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bampton C.E. Primary School - Extra-Curricular Activities
pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular Activities
As well as our own excellent After School Club we also have several high quality clubs that are running from external providers, and we are always looking at possibilities for new clubs that offer exciting extra curricular experiences and excellent value for money.
We currently have the following clubs running on a regular basis.
A variety of music lessons taught in small groups are available for parents and carers to purchase when children reach Key Stage two (Y3-Y6). These lessons take place at lunchtimes and are run by external music teachers.
Led by two of our Teaching Partners, our KS2 school choir are preparing to take part in Voice in a Million. The choir will also sing at various events throughout the year, including Bampton Garden Plants Christmas Shopping Evening.
Footy kids staff have experience of working within primary schools for over 10 years, delivering fun and exciting football clinics available to children in years 1-6 of primary school.
Sessions include fun exercises and matches to include every child according to the ability and age levels of the children which makes for an enjoyable learning experience.
Children experience the opportunity to play in realistic, age-specific small-sided football games.
An opportunity to be inspired to make your own creations.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bampton C.E. Primary School - Collective worship
pageCache.text:
Collective worship
As a Church of England school, we hold an inclusive and diverse daily act of Collective Worship.
We use several resources to support the planning and delivery of these 15-minute gatherings.
12 Christian values are explored in a 2 year programme of fully worked, creative material: Compassion, Courage, Forgiveness, Friendship, Generosity, Justice, Perseverance, Respect, Service, Thankfulness. Trust, Truthfulness.
Picture News finds the positives in current affairs by turning world events into learning opportunities. The assembly element explains the story, and includes additional open questions for meaningful discussion.
This provides an opportunity to reflect on the Picture News Big Questions in an age-appropriate way or sometimes explore something relevant to the class.
Once a week, the Reverend from the local church leads Collective Worship or a member of SLT will share a Heroes of Hope story (inspiring stories from Christians around the world)
These are linked to the PSHE theme for the half-term.
Friday Collective Worship promotes recognition of achievements (both in and out of school)and the celebration of birthdays.
These are part of a regular pattern of Collective Worship and allow us to focus on how our values are woven through all aspects of our school life.

Inspections
Latest Ofsted Report – January 2023
'Pupils thrive because of the high ambitions that radiate throughout the school. Classrooms are joyful and energetic places to be. Pupils show excitement and curiosity in their learning and are not afraid to try new things. Their resilience and confidence underpin the positive learning behaviours that they have.
In lessons, pupils understand what their teachers and teaching partners expect of them. Behaviour in the classroom is positive, and creates a calm and purposeful environment.
Leaders have ensured that all pupils have a strong start at Bampton CofE Primary School. Leaders have thought carefully about the knowledge their pupils need and when they need to learn it. Overall, there is a well-designed curriculum from Nursery onwards which aims to prepare pupils for their next steps as they progress through their education.
Pupils love to learn in this school. Their enthusiasm is clear to see and reflected in the positive way that they behave in lessons. Pupils’ behaviour supports learning very well. On the whole, all pupils, including those with SEND, fully gain the knowledge that their teachers intend them to learn. The strong culture and provision for pupils with SEND mean that successful adaptations are in place to ensure achievement for all.
In Nursery and Reception, staff are highly knowledgeable about the early years framework. They take every opportunity during the school day to talk to children and to develop their knowledge and vocabulary. Staff plan learning activities carefully, based on what they know children need to learn next. This highly effective planning means there are no limits to what children can achieve.'

Nursery
Childhood is a special time, and we are committed to making school life as happy and productive as possible for your child, and every child in our care.
At Bampton, we have a brand new purpose-built Early Years Unit, with 26 Nursery places alongside our 30 place Reception class.
Our Nursery offer, from the term after a child turns 3 years old, is 15 funded hours over five mornings (8:45-11:45am) or 30 funded hours across five days (8:45am-3:15pm)
Parents eligible for only 15 funded hours can purchase afternoon sessions.
If children are staying for the full school day, Parents and Carers will need to provide a packed lunch or book a school meal.
Parents and Carers are able to book Breakfast and After School Club for extended hours.
If you are interested in coming to view our excellent provision please contact the school office
Tel: 01993 850371 or email office.3131@bampton.oxon.sch.uk
